title: Deep-learning seismic catalog reveals a potentially reactivated blind fault in Taiwan’s 2025 Dapu earthquake sequence
summary: A RED-PAN deep-learning phase picker enabled a catalog of 6,805 relocated events for the 11-day sequence following the M6.4 Dapu earthquake. Analysis of those events, focal mechanisms and velocity structure identified an east-dipping plane at about 5–10 km and a west-dipping plane at about 10–15 km; the authors infer the mainshock involved a previously unrecognized blind west-dipping fault and interactions with the known Muchiliao–Liuchia system. This is a localized structural interpretation, and the authors describe some fault associations as potential.
organization: Academia Sinica; National Central University; National Taiwan University; Central Weather Administration of Taiwan

evidence.tested: A RED-PAN deep-learning phase picker enabled a catalog of 6,805 relocated events for the 11-day sequence following the M6.4 Dapu earthquake.
evidence.unknown: Peer-reviewed open-access short report. The principal west-dipping plane is interpreted as a potentially reactivated, previously unmapped blind fault; the paper calls some extended activity potential and recommends further monitoring. It is one earthquake sequence and the AI created the event catalog rather than independently deriving the tectonic model. A companion WTMA paper (DOI 10.1007/s44195-025-00095-9) analyzes the same Dapu sequence and similar two-plane geometry; it is a related, partly overlapping report and is not counted separately.
evidence.ai_role: RED-PAN detected P- and S-wave arrivals from continuous seismic recordings and supported event association and catalog construction; this catalog provided the relocated aftershock distribution used with focal mechanisms and velocity profiles to infer fault geometry. The fault interpretation itself involved human analysis, not an autonomous AI conclusion.
